headline: Steady sales growth, but margins get squeezed
summary_short: Net sales rose 1.8% year-over-year to $492.3 million, but operating income fell 26.8% to $84.4 million on tariffs, currency headwinds and a $32.2 million restructuring/software-abandonment charge tied partly to the Parse Biosciences integration.
summary_long: Sample technologies grew 13% (Parse Biosciences, automated kits) and EMEA rose 8%, but Diagnostic solutions fell 1% (QuantiFERON immigration-testing decline) and PCR/NAA fell 9% (Enzymes softness), leaving net sales up 1.8% y/y to $492.3M. Gross margin slipped to 62.9% from 63.8% on mix and tariffs/FX. Operating income fell 26.8% to $84.4M on $32.2M of restructuring/software-abandonment charges and higher Parse-related opex, partly offset by restructuring savings. Net income fell 25.0% to $68.0M despite a lower 20.7% tax rate. EPS fell 19.5% to $0.33, cushioned by fewer shares after the $496.7M synthetic repurchase. Cash fell to $646.3M from $839.0M on that repurchase. No FY2026 guidance was issued or restated.

drivers.explanation: Sample technologies +13% (Parse Biosciences contribution, automated kit sales) and EMEA +8% offset Diagnostic solutions -1% (QuantiFERON immigration-testing decline) and PCR/NAA -9% (Enzymes softness); FX added 3-4ppt across product groups.
Decrease to 62.9% from 63.8% primarily reflects product sales mix, plus the negative impact of tariffs and currency movements.
Tariffs and FX, higher Parse Biosciences-related opex, and $32.2M of restructuring/software-abandonment charges drove the decline, partly offset by restructuring-program efficiency gains.
Tracks the operating-income decline; partly cushioned by a lower effective tax rate (20.7% vs 24.1%) from favorable tax-structure benefits and lower expected top-up tax.
Follows net income's decline; partly offset by a lower diluted share count (208.9M vs 220.2M) after the January 2026 $496.7M synthetic share repurchase.
Decrease reflects increased working-capital requirements, including payments for efficiency measures and inventory build ahead of new product launches amid supply-chain caution.

Decline driven by $503.7M net cash used in financing (mainly the $496.7M synthetic repurchase capital repayment), partly offset by $211.5M from investing (short-term investment sales) and $100.6M from operations.
